entities.summary:
Zayn-e-Attar (d. 1403) was a 14th-century Persian physician renowned for authoring the influential pharmacopoeia Ekhtiyarat i Badi i. This comprehensive medical text, written in Persian, not only showcased Attar's expertise in traditional medicine but also played a crucial role in codifying Persian medical knowledge during the Islamic Golden Age. As a prominent figure in the field of medicine, Attar's work significantly contributed to the development of traditional Persian medicine, which continues to influence healthcare practices in the region to this day. His comprehensive pharmacopoeia has been studied and revered for centuries, with many of its recipes and treatments still in use today. Through his work, Attar not only advanced the field of medicine but also left a lasting legacy that continues to be felt in the world of healthcare.

In the Islamic world of the 14th century, Attar's expertise in medicine was highly valued, and his work was widely studied and respected. His pharmacopoeia, Ekhtiyarat i Badi i, was considered a masterpiece of Persian medical knowledge, and its impact can still be seen in the modern healthcare practices of the region. As a key figure in the development of traditional Persian medicine, Attar's contributions to the field have been recognized and celebrated for centuries.

Attar's legacy extends beyond the realm of medicine, as his work has also had a significant impact on the cultural and intellectual landscape of the Islamic world. His comprehensive pharmacopoeia has been a source of inspiration for many scholars and medical practitioners, and its influence can still be seen in the modern understanding of traditional medicine.
